s0101.literal: Soon he took the golden-wing [vessel] to help his father garrison Yingcheng.
s0101.idiomatic: Before long he sailed a golden-wing warship to help his father hold Yingcheng.

s0102.literal: When Hua Jiao was pacified, Lingxi and Wenji both had merit in defense.
s0102.idiomatic: After Hua Jiao was suppressed, both Lingxi and Wenji were credited with defensive merit.

s0103.literal: When Lingxi died, Wenji took full command of his troops; he was raised as Super Martial General and still helped defend Ying prefecture.
s0103.idiomatic: When Lingxi died, Wenji assumed command of all his troops, was made super-martial general, and continued to help defend Yingzhou.

s0104.literal: Wenji was by nature extremely filial; though campaigns set aside mourning rites, he wasted away from grief to an extreme degree.
s0104.idiomatic: Wenji was deeply filial; though active service set mourning aside, he grew emaciated with grief.

s0105.literal: In the second year of Taijian he was made Interior Secretary of Yuzhang; his general's rank was unchanged.
s0105.idiomatic: In Taijian year two he was appointed interior secretary of Yuzhang, keeping his general's rank.

s0106.literal: When mourning ended, he inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Chong'an county.
s0106.idiomatic: When mourning ended he inherited the dukedom of Chong'an county.

s0107.literal: He followed Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda leading troops to Jingzhou to campaign against Xiao Kui.
s0107.idiomatic: He followed Zhang Zhaoda, area commander, who led an army to Jingzhou against Xiao Kui.

s0108.literal: Kui and the Zhou army built many ships and placed them in the Qingni waters.
s0108.idiomatic: Kui and the Northern Zhou forces built many warships and anchored them in the Qingni channel.

s0109.literal: When the river was high and flowing fast, Zhaoda sent Wenji together with Qian Daozhi in light boats to attack, and they burned all the ships.
s0109.idiomatic: With the river swollen and swift, Zhaoda sent Wenji and Qian Daozhi in light craft to strike and burn the entire fleet.

s0110.literal: Zhaoda took advantage of Xiao Kui's troops growing slack and again sent Wenji by night into the outer city, inflicting very many casualties.
s0110.idiomatic: As Xiao Kui's men slackened, Zhaoda sent Wenji again by night into the outer city, killing many.

s0111.literal: Soon the Zhou army came out in force; Lei Daoqin, Interior Secretary of Baling, fought to the death in resistance; Wenji barely escaped with his life.
s0111.idiomatic: Northern Zhou then brought up its main force; Lei Daoqin, interior secretary of Baling, died fighting; Wenji barely escaped alive.

s0112.literal: For merit he was given Supernumerary Regular Attendant and Distant-Pacifying General, fief increased by five hundred households.
s0112.idiomatic: For merit he was made supernumerary regular attendant and distant-pacifying general, with five hundred added households.

s0113.literal: In year five, Area Commander Wu Mingche campaigned north against Qin commandery; before Qin commandery, Jiangpu connected with
s0113.idiomatic: In year five Wu Mingche, area commander, marched north against Qin commandery; upstream of the commandery Jiangpu joined

s0115.literal: [Tu] River; [3] the Qi men all drove great pillars as stakes to bar the water; he first sent Wenji leading picked braves to pull open the barrier; Mingche with the main army came from behind and attacked and took Qin commandery.
s0115.idiomatic: the Chu River. [3] Qi troops sank great pillars as stakes across the stream; Wenji was sent ahead with picked men to clear them, then Mingche brought the main force up and took Qin commandery.

s0116.literal: He also separately sent Wenji to besiege Jingzhou, slaughtered the city, advanced against Xuyi, and took it.
s0116.idiomatic: He also detached Wenji to invest Jingzhou, sacked the city, then advanced on Xuyi and captured it.

s0117.literal: He then followed Mingche in besieging Shouyang.
s0117.idiomatic: He then joined Mingche in the siege of Shouyang.

s0118.literal: Wenji in action was scrupulous and urgent, stern and orderly toward subordinates; fortresses he took before and after mostly dammed the water; earthworks often exceeded tens of thousands.
s0118.idiomatic: Wenji was exacting and quick in the field and strict with his men; every fortress he took he usually dammed with water, and the earthworks often ran to tens of thousands.

s0119.literal: Whenever camp labor was assigned, Wenji was ahead of the generals; at night he rose early and worked until evening without rest; none in the army failed to admire his diligence.
s0119.idiomatic: Whenever labor was set for the camp, Wenji outworked the other generals, rising before dawn and toiling until night; the whole army admired his industry.

s0120.literal: In every battle he was always vanguard; the Qi army deeply feared him and called him "Cheng the beast."
s0120.idiomatic: He always led the van in battle; Qi troops feared him deeply and nicknamed him "Cheng the beast."

s0121.literal: [4] For merit he was appointed Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and Bright-Martial General, fief increased by five hundred households.
s0121.idiomatic: [4] For merit he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and bright-martial general, with five hundred more households.

s0122.literal: He also acted as Interior Secretary of Xin'an and was advanced in title to Martial-Resolute General.
s0122.idiomatic: He also served as acting interior secretary of Xin'an and was promoted to martial-resolute general.

s0123.literal: In year eight he was made Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander over Qiao Province Military Affairs, Distant-Pacifying General, and Inspector of Qiao.
s0123.idiomatic: In year eight he received the staff, commanded armies in Qiao province as distant-pacifying general, and became inspector of Qiao.

s0124.literal: That same year he also commanded Beixu and Renzhou military affairs and was Inspector of Beixu; the rest unchanged.
s0124.idiomatic: That year he also took command of Beixu and Renzhou and became inspector of Beixu; his other posts were unchanged.

s0125.literal: In year nine he again followed Mingche north; they built a dam at Lüliang—the affair is told in Mingche's biography.
s0125.idiomatic: In year nine he again followed Mingche north and helped build the dam at Lüliang, as related in Mingche's biography.

s0126.literal: In spring of year ten they were defeated and Wenji was imprisoned by Zhou; he was nevertheless granted Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes.
s0126.idiomatic: In the spring of year ten the army was beaten; Wenji was taken by Zhou but was still given a mansion equal to the three dukes.

s0127.literal: In year eleven he escaped from Zhou; at Guoyang border guards seized him and sent him back to Chang'an; he died in prison.
s0127.idiomatic: In year eleven he fled Zhou, was seized by border guards at Guoyang, sent back to Chang'an, and died in prison.

s0128.literal: The Later Lord at the time had already broken with Zhou and did not know of it.
s0128.idiomatic: The Later Lord had already broken with Zhou and did not yet know.

s0129.literal: In the first year of Zhide the Later Lord first learned of it and posthumously made him Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant.
s0129.idiomatic: In Zhide year one the Later Lord learned of his fate and posthumously made him scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

s0130.literal: Soon another edict said: "The late Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and former Duke of Chong'an county and state lord Wenji inherited the gate-line and bore the family reputation.
s0130.idiomatic: Soon another edict declared: "The late scattered-cavalry regular attendant and former duke of Chong'an, Lord Wenji, upheld the family line and honored its name.

s0131.literal: In early years he went on campaign; though not commander-in-chief, in opening marches he was foremost and achieved results that were heard of; yet he lost chariots and followers and was allowed to be stripped of rank.
s0131.idiomatic: He took the field young; though not supreme commander, he led the van and won renown, yet lost men and transport and was rightly reduced in rank.

s0132.literal: Yet Lingxi's merits in defense are long remembered with longing; Wenji's soul buried in a foreign land is greatly to be pitied.
s0132.idiomatic: Lingxi's defensive service is long missed; Wenji lies abroad, which moves deep pity.

s0133.literal: Thinking of old merit and grieving this severance, temple sacrifices should be maintained—do not let them go wanting.
s0133.idiomatic: Recalling his service and grieving this break, his line should keep temple offerings and not be left without sacrifice.

s0134.literal: He may be demoted in enfeoffment to Marquis of Chong'an county, fief one thousand households; his son Xiang is to inherit the enfeoffment.
s0134.idiomatic: Let him be demoted to marquis of Chong'an with one thousand households, his son Xiang to inherit the title.

s0136.literal: The historiographer says: Cheng Lingxi father and son were both harsh toward subordinates and kept troops sternly disciplined, yet they shared toil with the masses and did not treat wealth as private profit; soldiers greatly relied on them—hence they succeeded whenever they took the field.
s0136.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Cheng Lingxi and his son were harsh masters and kept iron discipline, yet shared hardship with the ranks and took no private gain; men followed them willingly, and so they prevailed in war.

s0138.literal: His troops fought fiercely at Shitou's west gate—the Hall edition's textual verification says "troops" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "by night."
s0138.idiomatic: On "his troops fought fiercely at Shitou's west gate": the Hall edition notes that the Southern Dynasties history reads by night for troops.

s0139.literal: Now considered: it is suspected that "by night" is correct.
s0139.idiomatic: Present opinion: night is probably the correct reading.

s0140.literal: Summoned as Left Guard General—comment: in all editions the title was corrupt as rengshi general; now changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0140.idiomatic: On "summoned as left guard general": every edition had a corrupt title read as rengshi general; emended per the Southern Dynasties history.

s0141.literal: Before Qin commandery, Jiangpu connected with
s0141.idiomatic: Before Qin commandery, Jiangpu connected with

s0143.literal: [Tu] River—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Comprehensive Mirror.
s0143.idiomatic: [Tu] River—emended per the Southern Dynasties history and the Comprehensive Mirror.

s0144.literal: Comment: Tu River is Chu River; Hu's note to the Comprehensive Mirror says "Tu is read as Chu."
s0144.idiomatic: Note: Tu River is the Chu River; Hu's commentary to the Comprehensive Mirror reads tu as chu.

s0145.literal: Called "Cheng the beast"—comment: "beast" in the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions reads "tiger"; this avoids Tang taboo.
s0145.idiomatic: On "called Cheng the beast": Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read tiger, avoiding Tang taboo.

s0146.literal: Comment: The History of the Southern Dynasties changes "tiger" to "biao," also avoiding Tang taboo.
s0146.idiomatic: The Southern Dynasties history changes tiger to biao, likewise avoiding Tang taboo.

s0147.literal: His son Xiang to inherit the enfeoffment—the Hall edition's textual verification says "Xiang" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Xiang" (響).
s0147.idiomatic: On "his son Xiang to inherit": the Hall edition notes the Southern Dynasties history writes the name Xiang (響).
